name: regtab
description: RegTab matches tables the way RegEx matches text. RTL (Regular Table Language) is the table-pattern DSL of the RegTab project: syntax highlighting for .rtl files and for RTL embedded in Python and Java string literals, compiler diagnostics, live match preview against CSV fixtures, expected-result diffs, and Test Explorer integration.

rtl.fixtures.input.markdownDescription: A template that locates input CSV tables for a `.rtl` pattern, or an array of `{pattern, input}` rules. Variables: `${basename}` (pattern file name without extension), `${dir}` (its directory), and `${workspaceFolder}`. `${basename/regex/replacement/flags}` applies a snippet-style transform (for example, `${basename/RtlTask(.+)Test/task_$1/}` maps a host test file to its fixture directory). A `*` in the final path segment expands as a glob. Each rule's `pattern` is matched against the pattern file path; the first matching rule wins. Examples: `${dir}/${basename}.csv`; `[{"pattern": "solutions/regtab/*.rtl", "input": "${workspaceFolder}/fixtures/${basename}/input_*.csv"}]`.

rtl.fixtures.expected.markdownDescription: A template that locates expected-result CSV files for comparison with the extracted recordset, or an array of `{pattern, expected, hasHeader?, orderedRows?}` rules. Supports the same variables, final-segment glob, and first-match rule behavior as `#rtl.fixtures.input#`; the optional booleans override the global comparison settings for that rule. When expansion produces multiple files, the sorted expected files are paired positionally with the sorted input files; a single expected file applies to every input. An `// expected: path` directive inside the pattern takes precedence; expected and fixture directives are paired by position. Standalone `.rtl` patterns with an expected result also appear in the Test Explorer.

rtl.fixtures.expectedHasHeader.description: When enabled, the first row of an expected CSV contains column names and is compared positionally with the recordset schema; only the remaining rows are treated as data.

rtl.fixtures.orderedRows.description: When enabled, row order is significant when comparing the recordset with an expected CSV. Otherwise, rows are compared as an unordered multiset.

rtl.server.path.description: Path to an rtl-lsp executable. Overrides the server bundled with the extension (useful on platforms without a bundled binary).

rtl.trace.server.description: Trace the communication between VS Code and the RTL language server.

scripts.test: npm run check:types && npm run test:grammar && npm run test:unit && npm run check:sync
